items.headline: Yoshitha, ex-Navy chief plead not guilty
items.summary: Yoshitha Rajapaksa and former Navy Commander Wasantha Karannagoda pleaded not guilty in the Colombo High Court to bribery commission charges over Rajapaksa's 2006 placement at a British naval college. Further evidence will be taken on December 10.

items.headline: Pillayan remanded until December 7
items.summary: The Batticaloa Magistrate's Court kept former state minister Pillayan (Sivanesathurai Chandrakanthan) in remand. The CID has filed action against him and others over five killings in Batticaloa District in 2008.

items.headline: MEPA to seek compensation for port oil spill
items.summary: The Marine Environment Protection Authority will assess the damage from the Jaya Container Terminal diesel leak and claim compensation from those responsible. It says about 95% of the fuel flowing into the sea is now under control.

items.headline: Labour law overhaul presented to MPs
items.summary: Draft labour reforms covering contracts, working hours, overtime, and maternity and paternity leave were outlined to MPs. Four draft chapters of a Labour Standards Bill are open for public comment, and no law has been passed yet.

items.headline: Colombo–Kandy road shut overnight at Kadugannawa
items.summary: The main road at Lower Kadugannawa will be fully closed from 11 PM tonight to 6 AM tomorrow so that rocks at risk of falling can be removed. The DMC advises drivers to use alternative routes.

items.headline: Record tourist arrivals forecast for 2026
items.summary: Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath told Parliament that arrivals have passed two million and tourism earned US$2.3 billion by October. He expects close to 2.4 million visitors by year-end, which would be a new record.

items.headline: Opposition presses Govt in budget debate
items.summary: Namal Rajapaksa asked what happened to the US$4 billion Chinese investment announced after the President's China visit. Harsha de Silva proposed an "Asian Ocean" concept with Sri Lanka as a regional hub.

items.headline: Rights group calls anti-terror bill unworkable
items.summary: Justice for All told a parliamentary committee that the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Act should be withdrawn. It has also challenged the bill in the Supreme Court.

items.headline: Sri Lanka and Thailand exchange visa deal
items.summary: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake met Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister, and the two sides exchanged a visa-exemption agreement for ordinary passport holders. Thai reports describe it as allowing stays of up to 30 days.

items.headline: Weather in India may lift some import prices
items.summary: The Trade Minister warned that bad weather in India could raise prices of some imported goods. Importers say only dried chillies are affected, because shipments are exceeding the moisture limit.

items.headline: GSP+ talks led by special committee
items.summary: The Deputy Tourism Minister said a Cabinet-appointed committee is now leading discussions on renewing the EU's GSP+ trade concession.

items.headline: FitsAir resumes Colombo–Chennai flights
items.summary: The budget carrier has resumed direct flights between Colombo and Chennai.

items.headline: Chinese nationals fined Rs. 76.4m over Sinharaja
items.summary: Four Chinese nationals admitted to 143 charges of collecting protected wildlife in the Sinharaja buffer zone, and the Kalawana court fined them a total of Rs. 76.4 million. They were caught on November 9 with more than 300 protected animals.

items.headline: Heated exchange in Parliament over Ella trees
items.summary: Opposition MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake alleged that trees near the Ella playground were cut down to clear a hotel's view. Deputy Minister Ruwan Ranasinghe denied this, saying the old trees were a storm risk.

items.headline: Amber lightning warning for 17 districts
items.summary: The warning is in force until 11 PM tonight. It covers all of Colombo, Galle and Ratnapura and parts of Kandy and Puttalam, among other areas.

items.headline: National Sports Games titles decided
items.summary: At the 50th National Sports Games, Central and Southern provinces won the rugby sevens titles. North Western and Western provinces won gold in beach volleyball.

items.headline: Cricket's rulebook released in Sinhala and Tamil
items.summary: The Laws of Cricket are now available in both local languages.

items.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine hit Russian ships off Libya
items.summary: He said naval drones sank the warship Merkury and struck a cargo ship in Benghazi. The UN mission in Libya has called for an independent probe.

items.headline: Houthis claim strike on Saudi refinery
items.summary: The Houthis say they hit the Rabigh refinery on the Red Sea coast. The damage is unconfirmed, and Saudi Arabia has not commented.

items.headline: Zimbabwe arrests preacher Uebert Angel
items.summary: Police in Zimbabwe arrested the prominent pastor over sexual offence allegations.
